then.text: Come back Thursday, we do a lovely set. Bring a mate. Bring two. The club holds forty and there's always sixty.
Y'alright! Soundcheck's done and the band's gone for a pie. Fancy a rematch while it's quiet?

else.text: Once a day, mate. My arms need a rest from the drums and my team needs a rest from me. Tomorrow.
Another time, then. The offer stands.
Y'alright! Come in, come in, mind the amps. You've got the look of someone who's come all the way from the Peaks.
I'm Ray. I keep the Urban Stone here, and I do the odd drum solo. Mostly the Stone.
Let's see if you can keep time with the city. One, two, three, four!
This is the Urban Stone. Pavements, rooftops, pigeons. It's a city thing, so it's got a bit of grit.
And it'll teach your team Brook-wade. Deep water won't be a problem. Just don't wade the Mersey, mate. It's not that kind of deep.
{player}'s team learned Brook-wade! Deep water can now be crossed.
Your phone buzzes mid-solo. It's Professor Garside, who is clearly standing near a kettle.
{player}! The Urban Stone! Lovely. I felt it from here. Well, I felt my teacup rattle.
The hum is moving west now, into Wales. Dinas Emrys, Yr Wyddfa. The old dragon country.
I'm posting you a Rail Pass. Every station will let you hop between the towns you've visited. Don't lose it, it's laminated.
The Wirral road should be open. Head south to Chester, then west. And if you've a spare afternoon, there's a ferry to Douglas. The Manx are very polite about lost sheep.
Outside, the Wardens on the Wirral road quietly packed up their barriers and pretended it had been a drill.

liverpool_quizmaster.text: Right then, la, it's quiz night at the Cavern, or something very like it. Please put the guitars down, I can't hear myself think.
Five questions. Four answers each. The pub cat is the official scorer, and he cannot be bribed. I've tried.
Fancy a round? Five questions, no phones.

else.text: Fair play. Sound as a pound, you.
